verdict.rationale: iTerm2 documents a registrable system-wide hotkey that brings the terminal to the foreground. Its GitHub README describes a hotkey window that slides down from the top (or any edge), even over fullscreen apps. The features page explicitly likens this to Visor/Guake/Yakuake quake-style terminals. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of the hotkey/dropdown behavior.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can summon the terminal instantly with a global hotkey or quake-style dropdown window

citations.quote: Register a hotkey that brings iTerm2 to the foreground when you're in another application. A terminal is always a keypress away.
System-wide hotkey summons a terminal that slides down from the top of the screen (or any edge), even over fullscreen apps.
This gives you an always-available terminal (like Visor, Guake, or Yakuake) at your fingertips.
